conditions.summary: Three randomized trials settled the bridging question: routine heparin bridging around surgery in atrial fibrillation increases bleeding without preventing thromboembolism.
conditions.practice: Interrupt warfarin five days preoperatively and do not bridge unless thrombotic risk is genuinely high. For DOACs, a standardized interruption of 1 day before low-bleeding-risk and 2 days before high-bleeding-risk procedures needs no perioperative testing.
conditions.caveats: BRIDGE excluded mechanical valves and recent stroke, so the highest-risk patients most likely to need bridging are the ones the trial cannot speak to.

Perioperative Management of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving a Direct Oral Anticoagulant
Postoperative low molecular weight heparin bridging treatment for patients at high risk of arterial thromboembolism (PERIOP2): double blind randomised controlled trial

conditions.summary: Hydroxyurea remains the only disease-modifying therapy with mortality data. Voxelotor and crizanlizumab were approved on surrogate and crisis-rate endpoints, and both have since had their benefit questioned; gene therapies are curative-intent but new.
conditions.practice: Offer hydroxyurea to all patients with sickle cell anemia and recurrent crises; escalate to transfusion programs for stroke prevention. Treat newer agents as adjuncts, not replacements.
conditions.caveats: Voxelotor was withdrawn from the market in 2024 after post-approval data, a reminder that hemoglobin rise is not a clinical endpoint.

conditions.summary: Ravulizumab matched eculizumab with eight-weekly dosing; pegcetacoplan, acting proximally at C3, was superior to eculizumab for hemoglobin because it also prevents extravascular hemolysis.
conditions.practice: Choose a C5 inhibitor for intravascular hemolysis and thrombosis prevention; switch to or start proximal inhibition when residual anemia is driven by C3-opsonized extravascular clearance.
conditions.caveats: All complement inhibitors mandate meningococcal vaccination and carry a boxed warning; proximal inhibition may worsen breakthrough hemolysis if a dose is missed.

Pegcetacoplan versus Eculizumab in Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria

conditions.summary: For extended treatment after unprovoked VTE, reduced-dose DOACs preserve most of the efficacy of full dose with bleeding rates close to aspirin.
conditions.practice: After the first 6 months, continue apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily indefinitely for unprovoked proximal VTE, rather than stopping or dropping to aspirin.
conditions.caveats: Extension trials enrolled patients who had already tolerated 6-12 months of anticoagulation, so they under-represent early bleeders.

Apixaban for extended treatment of venous thromboembolism

conditions.summary: Randomized trials showed excess arterial thrombosis with rivaroxaban in triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome, reversing earlier enthusiasm for DOACs.
conditions.practice: Use warfarin, not a DOAC, in triple-positive APS and in any APS patient with arterial events. The 2023 ACR/EULAR criteria raised the laboratory bar for classification.
conditions.caveats: The 2023 criteria are classification, not diagnostic, criteria; a patient who fails them may still have the disease and need treatment.

The 2023 ACR/EULAR Antiphospholipid Syndrome Classification Criteria

conditions.summary: DOACs are now first-line for most cancer-associated VTE, but the gastrointestinal bleeding signal differs by agent and by tumour site.
conditions.practice: Apixaban is preferred when luminal gastrointestinal or genitourinary malignancy raises bleeding risk; edoxaban and rivaroxaban carry a higher GI bleeding rate in those patients. Low-molecular-weight heparin remains reasonable when absorption is unreliable.
conditions.caveats: CARAVAGGIO excluded primary brain tumours and acute leukemia, the two groups where the bleeding question is hardest.

conditions.summary: Emicizumab, a bispecific antibody bridging FIXa and FX, reduced bleeding by roughly 96 percent versus no prophylaxis and is given subcutaneously, decoupling prophylaxis from venous access.
conditions.practice: Emicizumab is standard prophylaxis for hemophilia A with or without inhibitors. Gene therapy offers durable factor expression but with variable, declining levels and hepatotoxicity requiring steroids.
conditions.caveats: Emicizumab invalidates one-stage aPTT-based FVIII assays; combining it with activated prothrombin complex concentrate caused thrombotic microangiopathy.

citations.title: Emicizumab Prophylaxis in Patients Who Have Hemophilia A without Inhibitors
Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec Gene Therapy for Hemophilia A

conditions.summary: The 2019 ASH guidelines moved away from prolonged corticosteroids and towards early second-line therapy with thrombopoietin receptor agonists or rituximab.
conditions.practice: Limit initial corticosteroids to no more than six weeks including taper. Choose between TPO-RAs, rituximab and splenectomy by patient preference, comorbidity and desire for durable remission off therapy.
conditions.caveats: Platelet count is a poor proxy for bleeding risk; treat the bleeding phenotype, not the number.

citations.title: American Society of Hematology 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia

conditions.summary: Management of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia rests on pretest probability scoring and immediate substitution with a non-heparin anticoagulant, not on waiting for confirmatory assays.
conditions.practice: Stop all heparin and start argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC at the point of intermediate or high 4Ts score. Do not give prophylactic platelet transfusions, and delay warfarin until platelets recover.
conditions.caveats: A positive immunoassay alone over-diagnoses HIT; a functional assay is needed to confirm, and the 4Ts score is what should drive the immediate action.

citations.title: American Society of Hematology 2018 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia

conditions.summary: Caplacizumab, an anti-VWF nanobody, shortened time to platelet normalization and reduced refractory disease and recurrence when added to plasma exchange and immunosuppression.
conditions.practice: Start plasma exchange and corticosteroids immediately on clinical suspicion; add rituximab and consider caplacizumab. ADAMTS13 activity confirms the diagnosis but must not delay exchange.
conditions.caveats: Caplacizumab increases mucocutaneous bleeding and mortality benefit was not demonstrated; it does not treat the underlying autoimmunity, so relapse follows withdrawal if ADAMTS13 has not recovered.

conditions.summary: Restrictive transfusion thresholds are non-inferior across most settings, with myocardial infarction the notable exception where the evidence remains unsettled.
conditions.practice: Transfuse at a hemoglobin of 7 g/dL for most hospitalized patients and 8 g/dL after cardiac surgery or with pre-existing cardiovascular disease. Single-unit orders with reassessment are the default.
conditions.caveats: MINT found a non-significant trend favouring liberal transfusion in myocardial infarction, so the 7 g/dL threshold should not be applied reflexively there.

citations.title: Transfusion requirements in critical care (TRICC): a multicentre, randomized, controlled clinical study. Transfusion Requirements in Critical Care Investigators and the Canadian Critical care Trials Group
Restrictive or Liberal Transfusion Strategy in Myocardial Infarction and Anemia

conditions.summary: Post-transplant cyclophosphamide improved GVHD-free relapse-free survival even in HLA-matched transplants, and ruxolitinib beat best available therapy in steroid-refractory GVHD.
conditions.practice: Post-transplant cyclophosphamide with tacrolimus and mycophenolate is now a standard prophylaxis backbone beyond the haploidentical setting. Ruxolitinib is first-line for steroid-refractory acute and chronic GVHD.
conditions.caveats: Ruxolitinib response rates are high but durable complete responses are less common, and cytopenias and infection limit dosing.

citations.title: Post-Transplantation Cyclophosphamide-Based Graft-versus-Host Disease Prophylaxis
Ruxolitinib for Glucocorticoid-Refractory Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease

conditions.summary: CD19 CAR T-cell therapy produced durable remissions in chemorefractory large B-cell lymphoma and has since moved into second line, beating salvage chemotherapy plus autologous transplant.
conditions.practice: Refer patients relapsing within 12 months of first-line therapy for second-line CAR T rather than salvage chemotherapy and transplant. Manage cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity by grading, with tocilizumab and steroids.
conditions.caveats: Trials enrolled patients fit enough for transplant; outcomes in older or frailer patients, and the sequencing question against bispecific antibodies, remain open.

citations.title: Axicabtagene Ciloleucel CAR T-Cell Therapy in Refractory Large B-Cell Lymphoma
Axicabtagene Ciloleucel as Second-Line Therapy for Large B-Cell Lymphoma

conditions.summary: Imatinib transformed CML into a chronic disease; second-generation TKIs achieve deeper molecular responses faster but have not translated that into an overall survival advantage.
conditions.practice: Any approved first-line TKI is acceptable; choose by comorbidity and by whether treatment-free remission is a goal. Monitor BCR::ABL1 by international-scale PCR at 3, 6 and 12 months against milestone targets.
conditions.caveats: Nilotinib carries vascular occlusive risk and dasatinib pleural effusion; a deeper molecular response is only worth an added toxicity if discontinuation is actually the plan.

citations.title: Imatinib compared with interferon and low-dose cytarabine for newly diagnosed chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia
Nilotinib versus imatinib for newly diagnosed chronic myeloid leukemia

conditions.summary: Asciminib binds the myristoyl pocket rather than the ATP site, giving activity after ATP-competitive TKI failure with a better safety profile than ponatinib.
conditions.practice: Test for kinase-domain mutations at failure. T315I demands ponatinib or asciminib at higher dose; response-adjusted ponatinib dosing reduces arterial occlusive events without losing efficacy.
conditions.caveats: Asciminib was compared with bosutinib, not with ponatinib, so the two are not ranked against each other by randomized evidence.

citations.title: Asciminib in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia after ABL Kinase Inhibitor Failure

conditions.summary: About half of patients in sustained deep molecular response stay in remission after stopping a TKI, and most who relapse regain response on restarting.
conditions.practice: Consider discontinuation after at least 3 years of therapy and 2 years of MR4 or deeper, with monthly PCR for the first 6 months. Restart on loss of major molecular response.
conditions.caveats: Roughly a quarter develop a transient TKI withdrawal syndrome of musculoskeletal pain; discontinuation outside a monitoring programme with reliable international-scale PCR is unsafe.

citations.title: Discontinuation of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy in chronic myeloid leukaemia (EURO-SKI): a prespecified interim analysis of a prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, trial

conditions.summary: A hematocrit target below 45 percent halved cardiovascular death and major thrombosis, and ruxolitinib controls hydroxyurea-resistant or intolerant disease.
conditions.practice: Phlebotomize to a hematocrit below 45 percent and give low-dose aspirin to all. Add cytoreduction for age over 60 or prior thrombosis; ruxolitinib is second-line after hydroxyurea failure.
conditions.caveats: The 45 percent threshold comes from a single open-label trial with a modest event count; the target has not been re-tested.

citations.title: Cardiovascular events and intensity of treatment in polycythemia vera
Ruxolitinib versus standard therapy for the treatment of polycythemia vera

conditions.summary: JAK inhibitors reduce spleen size and symptoms in myelofibrosis without altering the disease's clonal course; momelotinib uniquely improves anemia through ACVR1 inhibition.
conditions.practice: Select the JAK inhibitor by the dominant problem: ruxolitinib for spleen and symptoms, momelotinib when anemia and transfusion dependence dominate, pacritinib when platelets are below 50. Allogeneic transplant remains the only curative option.
conditions.caveats: Stopping ruxolitinib abruptly can precipitate a cytokine rebound syndrome; taper rather than stop.

conditions.summary: Adding eltrombopag to horse antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine raised complete response rates and shortened time to response in severe aplastic anemia.
conditions.practice: Horse ATG plus cyclosporine plus eltrombopag is first-line for patients who are not transplant candidates. Matched sibling transplant remains first-line for younger patients.
conditions.caveats: Rabbit ATG is inferior to horse ATG in this disease, a distinction that is easy to get wrong when substituting products.

citations.title: Eltrombopag Added to Immunosuppression in Severe Aplastic Anemia

conditions.summary: IPSS-M incorporates 31 mutated genes alongside cytogenetics and blood counts, and restratifies roughly half of patients compared with IPSS-R.
conditions.practice: Send a myeloid mutation panel at diagnosis and calculate IPSS-M, not IPSS-R alone, before deciding on transplant referral or hypomethylating therapy.
conditions.caveats: IPSS-M was derived largely in patients not receiving disease-modifying therapy, so it predicts natural history better than it predicts treatment response.

citations.title: Molecular International Prognostic Scoring System for Myelodysplastic Syndromes

conditions.summary: Azacitidine improved survival in higher-risk MDS; luspatercept reduces transfusion burden in lower-risk disease and outperformed epoetin alfa in the first-line setting.
conditions.practice: Split management by risk. Lower-risk: treat the cytopenia, with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents or luspatercept, and lenalidomide for del(5q). Higher-risk: hypomethylating agent with early transplant referral for fit patients.
conditions.caveats: Luspatercept improves transfusion independence but has never been shown to change survival or progression to AML.

citations.title: Luspatercept in Patients with Lower-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes
Efficacy of azacitidine compared with that of conventional care regimens in the treatment of higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: a randomised, open-label, phase III study

conditions.summary: AML management is now genomically directed: ELN 2022 restratified risk, and adding midostaurin to intensive chemotherapy improved survival in FLT3-mutated disease.
conditions.practice: Send rapid FLT3 and NPM1 testing before starting therapy so a targeted agent can be added to induction. Use measurable residual disease to guide consolidation and transplant.
conditions.caveats: ELN 2022 risk groups were derived in intensively treated patients and perform poorly for patients receiving venetoclax-based therapy.

citations.title: Midostaurin plus Chemotherapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia with a FLT3 Mutation

conditions.summary: Azacitidine plus venetoclax roughly doubled median survival versus azacitidine alone in patients ineligible for intensive chemotherapy, and has become the standard of care in that group.
conditions.practice: Offer azacitidine-venetoclax to patients unfit for intensive induction. Plan a marrow at the end of cycle 1, hold venetoclax for count recovery, and adjust dose for azole antifungals.
conditions.caveats: IDH1/2 and NPM1 mutations respond particularly well while TP53 does not, so a single median survival figure conceals very different trajectories.

citations.title: Azacitidine and Venetoclax in Previously Untreated Acute Myeloid Leukemia

conditions.summary: Brentuximab vedotin with AVD improved survival over ABVD in advanced Hodgkin lymphoma, and nivolumab-AVD subsequently beat brentuximab-AVD on progression-free survival with less toxicity.
conditions.practice: Nivolumab-AVD is emerging as the preferred front-line regimen in advanced-stage disease. Bleomycin is omitted in most modern regimens because of pulmonary toxicity.
conditions.caveats: S1826 reported early progression-free survival; overall survival and late effects, which matter enormously in a young curable population, are not yet mature.

citations.title: Brentuximab vedotin with chemotherapy for stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma (ECHELON-1): 5-year update of an international, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial

conditions.summary: Bispecific antibodies produce high complete response rates in heavily pretreated follicular lymphoma with off-the-shelf availability, competing with CAR T-cell therapy.
conditions.practice: For relapsed follicular lymphoma, weigh bispecifics, CAR T and lenalidomide-rituximab by prior lines, fitness and access. Watch for early progression within 24 months, which marks a poor-risk group.
red_flags: Progression within 24 months of first therapy
conditions.caveats: Response rates come from single-arm trials; no randomized comparison establishes bispecifics against CAR T in this disease.

citations.title: Safety and efficacy of mosunetuzumab, a bispecific antibody, in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: a single-arm, multicentre, phase 2 study

conditions.summary: POLARIX showed a progression-free survival advantage for polatuzumab-R-CHP over R-CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL, without an overall survival difference.
conditions.practice: Consider polatuzumab-R-CHP for IPI 2 or higher, particularly non-germinal-centre subtypes. R-CHOP remains an acceptable standard, and cell-of-origin plus MYC/BCL2 rearrangement status should be established up front.
conditions.caveats: The absolute progression-free survival gain was about 6 percent with no survival benefit, and subgroup benefit was inconsistent.

citations.title: Polatuzumab Vedotin in Previously Untreated Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma

conditions.summary: For DLBCL relapsing within 12 months, CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is superior to salvage chemotherapy with autologous transplant.
conditions.practice: Split relapsed disease by timing. Early relapse or primary refractory: CAR T. Late relapse in a transplant-fit patient: salvage chemotherapy and autologous transplant remain reasonable.
conditions.caveats: One second-line CAR T trial was negative, and the differences between products and between trial designs matter more than the shared headline.

citations.title: Lisocabtagene maraleucel versus standard of care with salvage chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation as second-line treatment in patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma (TRANSFORM): results from an interim analysis of an open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial

conditions.summary: Chemoimmunotherapy has been displaced in front-line CLL by continuous BTK inhibition and by fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab.
conditions.practice: Test IGHV mutation status and TP53 aberration before treating. Choose between fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab and continuous BTK inhibition by comorbidity, cardiac risk and patient preference for a defined stopping point.
conditions.caveats: Second-generation BTK inhibitors reduced cardiac toxicity relative to ibrutinib but the trials are not powered for survival differences between them.

Acalabrutinib with or without obinutuzumab versus chlorambucil and obinutuzmab for treatment-naive chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (ELEVATE TN): a randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial

conditions.summary: Fixed-duration venetoclax-rituximab beat bendamustine-rituximab in relapsed CLL, and non-covalent BTK inhibition with pirtobrutinib retains activity after covalent BTK inhibitor failure including BTK C481S.
conditions.practice: At relapse, switch mechanism class rather than repeating it. Pirtobrutinib and BTK degraders are options after covalent BTK inhibitor failure; CAR T is reserved for double-refractory disease.
conditions.caveats: Pirtobrutinib was approved on single-arm response data; durability after covalent BTK failure is still being defined.

Pirtobrutinib after a Covalent BTK Inhibitor in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia

conditions.summary: Adding an anti-CD38 antibody to bortezomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone deepens response and prolongs progression-free survival, and autologous transplant still adds progression-free but not overall survival benefit.
conditions.practice: Quadruplet induction with daratumumab or isatuximab is the standard for transplant-eligible patients, followed by autologous transplant and lenalidomide maintenance. Risk-adapt maintenance for high-risk cytogenetics.
conditions.caveats: DETERMINATION found no overall survival gain from early transplant and more second primary malignancies, so deferring transplant to first relapse remains defensible.

citations.title: Daratumumab, Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma
Triplet Therapy, Transplantation, and Maintenance until Progression in Myeloma

conditions.summary: BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibodies have moved into earlier relapse, with ciltacabtagene autoleucel superior to standard triplets in lenalidomide-refractory disease.
conditions.practice: In lenalidomide-refractory relapse, refer for BCMA CAR T where available. Bispecifics targeting BCMA or GPRC5D are off-the-shelf alternatives; both carry substantial infection risk requiring immunoglobulin support and prophylaxis.
red_flags: Delayed neurotoxicity or parkinsonism after CAR T
conditions.caveats: Manufacturing time and slot availability mean CAR T is not an option for rapidly progressing disease, which is precisely where it is most wanted.

citations.title: Cilta-cel or Standard Care in Lenalidomide-Refractory Multiple Myeloma
Teclistamab in Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma

conditions.summary: Adding daratumumab to cyclophosphamide-bortezomib-dexamethasone roughly doubled the hematologic complete response rate and improved organ response in AL amyloidosis.
conditions.practice: Daratumumab-CyBorD is first-line for newly diagnosed AL amyloidosis. Stage by cardiac biomarkers, because early mortality is driven by cardiac involvement rather than by clonal burden.
conditions.caveats: ANDROMEDA excluded the highest-risk cardiac stage, exactly the group with the worst outcomes and the least evidence.

citations.title: Daratumumab-Based Treatment for Immunoglobulin Light-Chain Amyloidosis

conditions.summary: Zanubrutinib showed fewer atrial fibrillation events than ibrutinib in Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and MYD88 and CXCR4 genotype predicts BTK inhibitor response.
conditions.practice: Genotype MYD88 and CXCR4 before choosing therapy. BTK inhibitors are highly effective in MYD88-mutated disease; MYD88 wild-type responds poorly and favours chemoimmunotherapy.
conditions.caveats: ASPEN was designed around a MYD88-mutated population; the wild-type cohort was small and non-randomized.
